+The integration fixture's numerator probe is deliberately factorized:
+
+\[
+  \bigl(Q_4^0+m\bigr)\bigl(Q_5^0-2m\bigr).
+
+\]
+
+The physical analyzer retains these as two separate linear edge dependencies;
+it does not first expand their product or replace them by an LMB polynomial.
+
+The analytic companion test then uses the sharper single-channel probe
+
+\[
+  (Q_5^0)^2.
+\]
+
+All three exact cubic occurrences share the relevant algebraic energy, but
+this quadratic probe is an original numerator factor. It retains its canonical
+source occurrence and supplies one degree-two bound, as the companion test
+explicitly requires. Only newly denominator-derived factors may enter the
+bounded dispatch search. No expanded quadratic polynomial is constructed.
+
+The unit test `exact_cff_cubic_uv_rewrite_matches_production_convention` uses the
+source-compatible routing `(4:+Q,5:+Q,7:-Q)` and permutes the input factor order.
+For every order it verifies:
+
+- a valid momentum-balanced exact graph;
+- one active topological loop;
+- no spurious causal surface from the zero-denominator cograph component;
+- complete signed CFF values independent of input factor order;
+- the analytic cubic-pole production contour
+  \(3i/(128\pi^3E^5)\);
+- complete contours for original and derivative-created quadratic factors,
+  retaining their distinct ownership domains;
+- the correct lower-sector parity for a `q_0^2` numerator,
+  \(-i/(128\pi^3E^3)\); and
+- the temporal/spatial cancellation of a full `q^2` numerator.

+The mirrored fixture
+[`scalar_mirrored_cubic_exact_uv_rewrite.dot`](../../tests/resources/graphs/uv_tests/scalar_mirrored_cubic_exact_uv_rewrite.dot)
+reverses edge 5 and changes the inner carrier so that the leading routing is

+\[
+  Q,\quad -Q,\quad -Q.
+
+\]

+Both fixtures are exercised through three production routes:
+
+1. orientation-local direct local 3D UV;
+2. direct local 3D UV with an explicit orientation sum; and
+3. local 4D UV followed by exact CFF projection and an explicit orientation
+   sum.

+The first two routes are parity comparators and do not use the lifting described
+in this document: they apply Taylor operators after complete/global CFF energy
+integration and differ only by selector omission. Only route 3 reconstructs
+exact source occurrences and performs bounded EMR dispatch.

+They are compared at several small and large momentum points. The strongest
+comparison evaluates the explicit-local-3D and projected-local-4D routes

+to precision loss in the precision-escalation path. Because the two real graph

+original and mirrored UV cycles contain `Q/Q/-Q` and `Q/-Q/-Q` respectively,

+## Complete example 7: the `epem_a_ddx` GL0 self-energy source
+
+The scalar fixtures isolate the mechanism, but the motivating production case
+is the NLO `epem_a_ddx` self-energy graph GL0.
+
+Structured generation traces show two different stages:
+
+| Source | Physical source-edge EMR bounds |
+| --- | --- |
+| GL0 ordinary full graph | `[(2,1),(3,1),(5,1),(7,1)]` |
+| GL2 ordinary full graph | `[(2,1),(3,1),(5,1),(6,1)]` |
+| GL0 contracted integrated-UV source | `[(2,1),(3,2),(5,1)]` |
+| GL2 first contracted integrated-UV source | `[(2,1),(3,1)]` |
+| GL2 second contracted integrated-UV source | `[(5,1),(6,1)]` |
+
+Thus the only genuinely raised physical EMR dependency is the quadratic bound
+on edge 3 in the contracted GL0 source. The two propagator edges adjacent to
+the self-energy insertion are physically related, but after the vakint result
+and its external EMR shift are remapped, edge 3 deterministically owns the
+remaining quadratic dependency; edge 5 remains linear. This is a physical-EMR
+provenance decision, not an LMB choice.
+
+The physical degree-two bound is not itself permission to redistribute its
+factors. A completed local-4D term retains original factors on their source
+occurrences. If new denominator-derived factors have two eligible serial
+copies, the rank baseline may propose `(1,1)`; the native map-row comparison
+then selects among the bounded proposals. The physical-source trace above
+neither records that selected occurrence plan nor proves its map count.
+
+GL2 supplies a useful contrast. Both of its contracted integrated-UV sources
+remain linear, as expected for the triangle correction which factorizes the
+Born graph. The GL0/GL2 comparison therefore tests that the generalized energy
+machinery is activated only where the self-energy numerator actually requires
+it.
+
+`State::generation_summary(...)` exposes contracted-source diagnostics in each
+graph report's `stats.cff_energy_degree_bound_reports` field.
+The DDx acceptance reads those reports and distinguishes the physical parent
+bounds from exact-source assigned bounds. They are generation diagnostics,
+separate from the ordinary graph retained by `ProcessIntegrand`; acceptance
+checks should use this summary rather than infer transient bounds from the
+final evaluator.

+## Generalized-CFF behavior after the lift
+
+Once the exact parsed graph and occurrence bounds have been produced, the
+shared `three-dimensional-reps` crate handles generalized residues. Its focused
+fixtures cover:
+
+- a repeated box with branching denominator trees;
+- one-loop quadratic, cubic, and quartic completions;
+- `box_pow3` with repeated quadratic recursive contact and remainder sectors;
+- repeated high-power channels with a common auxiliary sampling scale `M`;
+- multi-loop sunrise powers and penta contact sectors;
+- several choices of which `Q/Q/-Q` occurrence owns an equivalent bound; and
+- retention of distinct affine maps even when two terms have the same coarse
+  orientation.
+
+In particular, the shared-core fixture
+`cff_repeated_occurrence_bounds_preserve_equivalent_physical_numerators`
+compares the complete signed scalar and quadratic functions requested by
+
+```text
+(3,2), (4,2), (5,2),
+(3,1)+(4,1), (3,1)+(5,1), (4,1)+(5,1)
+```
+
+on a repeated `Q/Q/-Q` denominator at two deterministic points. The fixture
+reverses both endpoints and the full momentum signature, verifies the graph,
+and includes the reversed numerator sign. Each representation acts on the
+factor-local polynomial class specified by its bounds; equivalent physical
+numerators must yield the same complete function. Separate analytic quadratic
+and quartic contours retain independent mathematical oracles.
+GammaLoop's exact source normalizes denominator signatures and restores the raw
+sign in its separate numerator mapper.
+
+Higher-degree reconstruction interpolates one occurrence at a time and divides
+each interpolation basis polynomial only by that occurrence's denominator.
+Contracting that edge passes an exact, factorized quotient to the existing
+lower-sector CFF completion. It does not replace several equal denominators by a
+single powered channel or impose a common sampling node on their numerators.
+
+When a bound exceeds the direct interpolation range, generalized CFF may sample
+an EMR energy as a signed integer multiple `a*M` of the common auxiliary scale.
+This remains an occurrence-local EMR substitution. It is never an LMB rewrite,
+and the final physical expression is required to be independent of the nonzero
+value chosen for `M`.
+
+## Why the construction is generic
+
+The confidence claim is deliberately scoped: the construction is generic for
+the factorized polynomial EMR numerators and rational denominator powers
+produced by GammaLoop's local UV machinery. It is not a claim that every
+arbitrary symbolic function can be projected without certification.
+
+Within that production class, genericity follows from the following properties.
+
+### 1. Denominator multiplicity is arbitrary
+
+Any representable negative integer power becomes the corresponding number of
+occurrences of its rewritten denominator. The serial-chain constructor accepts
+an arbitrary raised-wrapper multiplicity and adds exactly one fewer auxiliary
+vertices. Algebraically coincident occurrences retain separate bounds and
+samples regardless of how many distinct owners supplied them. No power-two or
+GL0 branch exists in the implementation.
+
+### 2. Skeleton recovery is source-backed and rational identity is owner-free
+
+The source edge and its cograph/UV minor provide the original skeleton,
+component domain, and attachment for every process and UV-spinney shape. This
+sidesteps the generic inverse problem of deriving graph incidence from momentum
+signatures. Within one raised source wrapper, domain, exact momentum signature
+up to sign, and mass must agree. Across owners, the same normalized signature
+and mass identify the same rational channel. Relabeling compatible owners can
+change physical provenance, but not the channel's residue or loop rank.
+
+### 3. Canonicalization is topology-preserving
+
+Cograph and UV graph minors are constructed directly from the physical source,
+including contraction of absent edges. Explicit crown hedges retain non-vacuum
+external boundaries. Only after this scaffold exists does the owner-blind
+occurrence lift and Graphica relabeling establish deterministic rational
+equality and caching. No signature matroid, Kirchhoff system, or incidence
+search is part of exact-source topology construction.
+
+The rank solve at source-topology validation is the two-candidate quotient-space test
+for the routing sign of an already attached owner: `exact_row -/+ source_row`
+must lie in the span of the opposite source domain. It returns one unique
+`+1` or `-1`, or fails. It cannot propose endpoints, connect components, or
+synthesize an edge to repair vertex balance.
+
+### 4. Numerator degree composition is structural
+
+The analyzer implements polynomial composition rules over sums, products,
+powers, dot products, and multilinear functions. It does not recognize a
+particular numerator string or expand it into process-specific monomials.
+
+### 5. Actual native map rows select among certified rank proposals
+
+Rank/Pareto planning retains fixed owner loads and the factorized sum/product
+rules. Comparing descending envelopes proposes balanced lower degrees even when
+another occurrence fixes the maximum; quotient/remainder balancing is its
+special case for freely assignable unit factors. The production choice uses
+actual native source-map rows among K<=3 certified proposals, with rank and
+deterministic order breaking count ties. This restricted proposal class does
+not imply a globally minimal map count.
+
+### 6. Bound and evaluation cannot diverge
+
+One assignment object drives both generalized-CFF bounds and later numerator
+substitutions. Generic future terms cannot accidentally take a different
+mapping path after their bounds have been certified.
+
+Batching does not weaken this statement. Reuse requires equal canonical
+topology and identical per-occurrence capacity, while each term still evaluates
+through its own factor-local plan. Canonical topology identity includes
+external edges and affine boundary data, so reuse remains valid for disconnected
+and non-vacuum exact sources as well as vacuum UV factors.
+
+### 7. Routing signs are first-class data
+
+Canonicalization up to sign normalizes the denominator signature stored in the
+parsed graph. A rational-routing component then receives one coherent canonical
+direction, which can reverse that intermediate spelling. The numerator mapper
+composes the separate literal occurrence sign with the final parsed-routing
+sign and restores the physical numerator convention. This works for odd, even,
+scalar, and tensor numerator factors.
+
+### 8. Provenance projection is channel-complete
+
+Owner relabeling does not erase physical information. Occurrence-energy maps
+retain the particular source owner, while neutral cut support is the set union
+of all distinct owners in the algebraic channel. The union automatically
+deduplicates repeated copies of one owner and extends to any channel
+multiplicity. Adding raised-group representatives preserves compatibility with
+physical cut selection without replacing that owner set. None of these rules
+depends on a bubble, triangle, GL0, or a particular number of raised edges.
+
+### 9. Unsupported cases fail closed
+
+The implementation returns contextual errors for:
+
+- a non-integer or unsupported energy-dependent denominator power;
+- an opaque nonlinear energy function;
+- a physical EMR degree with no certified literal exact occurrence;
+- duplicate or overlapping candidate ownership;
+- one source edge instantiating incompatible normalized denominators in an
+  additive term;
+- a source-backed exact topology which violates loop-momentum conservation; and
+- a rank which has no valid source-carrier basis.
+
+Failing instead of selecting a convenient owner or LMB coordinate is part of
+the genericity guarantee: adding a more complicated nested self-energy cannot
+silently fall through to a test-specific approximation.
+
+## Minimality and runtime consequences
+
+The design minimizes work at three levels.
+
+First, the graph lift is minimal: a power `r` requires exactly `r` occurrences,
+and raising one source wrapper requires `r-1` auxiliary subdivision vertices.
+It does not clone the surrounding graph or algebraically cancel
+numerator/denominator pairs upstream.
+
+Second, the numerator lift compares actual native map rows for a small set of
+rank-ordered proposals. Assigning four eligible new hard unit factors as
+`(2,2)` instead of `(4,0)` can reduce reconstruction/contact work, but topology
+and complete-map coalescing determine the actual count. The bounded search may
+prefer a less balanced proposal when it produces fewer rows. Original factors
+remain fixed, and soft routing uses its separate exact off-shell certificate.
+The additional contender has a generation cost of its own; a net runtime or
+memory benefit requires measurements rather than an envelope-only argument.
+All proposal and selection work preserves the factorized numerator.
+
+Third, retaining natural Taylor denominator topologies avoids artificially
+raised propagator powers and compensating numerator factors. Canonical batching
+reuses expressions only for equal topology and identical per-occurrence capacity,
+avoiding rank inflation across independent terms. The real degree-one triangle
+therefore presents its base and singly dotted terms as separate source
+topologies, each with its own factorized numerator and capacity.
+
+For genuine numerator factors, upstream algebraic cancellation such as
+`D(Q)/D(Q)^2 -> 1/D(Q)` is deliberately not performed. Supplying the proper
+occurrence bounds lets generalized CFF perform the required pinches and
+lower-sector reconstruction internally. Preserving natural Taylor topologies
+does not require such cancellation: it avoids creating the compensating factors
+in the first place, without making source incidence depend on process-specific
+numerator simplification.
+
+## Maintained invariants
+
+Future changes to this path should preserve all of the following:
+
+1. A denominator occurrence is never dropped merely because another occurrence
+   has the same owner.
+2. The original `EdgeIndex` survives the Taylor operator as `source_edge`.
+3. Source owners and the original graph determine the contracted cograph/UV
+   scaffold and physical attachments; signatures never reconstruct that
+   skeleton or choose original endpoints.
+4. Compatible owner-relabeling comparisons require valid source-backed lifts
+   on both sides, with the same topology domain, mass and `D(Q)=D(-Q)` channel.
+   Their equal rational residue is not permission to infer incidence from
+   denominators or to move an original numerator factor off its retained owner.
+5. Raising one source wrapper produces the requested occurrence multiplicity
+   through minimal serial subdivision; the owner's label is not subsequently
+   part of rational CFF identity.
+6. UV and cograph denominator node domains never merge.
+7. Repeated occurrences of one owner must have the same normalized signature
+   and mass, or generation fails.
+8. `+Q` and `-Q` share a normalized denominator signature, while the literal
+   sign and any later coherent component reversal are composed separately for
+   physical-numerator mapping.
+9. The quotient-space rank calculation can choose only the unique routing sign
+   on fixed source endpoints; it cannot reconstruct or repair incidence.
+10. Occurrence-energy projection retains the particular physical owner which
+    supplied each occurrence, independently of owner-free rational incidence.
+11. Cut support for an exact algebraic channel is the sorted, deduplicated union
+    of all distinct physical owners which instantiate that channel.
+12. Raised-edge representative aliases are added to unioned cut support for LU
+    compatibility; they never replace or erase the original physical owners.
+13. A physical numerator `Q` is reconstructed with the physical sign even when
+   assigned to a `-Q` occurrence.
+14. Numerator energy degrees are computed solely in physical EMR variables.
+15. LMB coordinates never own an energy bound or serve as an identity fallback.
+16. The numerator remains factorized through analysis and mapping.
+17. The same immutable per-term plan owns bounds and substitutions.
+18. CFF cache reuse requires equal topology and identical per-occurrence bounds.
+    Bounds of degenerate occurrences are never summed or redistributed;
+    independent terms retain their own plans.
+19. Additive branches reuse capacity; multiplicative and multilinear slots
+    consume capacity.
+20. Lower-sector pinching does not reassign a factor away from its certified
+    occurrence.
+21. Input factor order does not alter the canonically relabeled exact source;
+    changing only a compatible physical owner changes provenance, not the
+    rational graph or residue.
+22. Non-vacuum external boundaries remain explicit source-crown hedges.
+23. No internal edge or external-balance edge is synthesized from momentum
+    signatures; an inconsistent source-backed graph fails validation.
+24. Unsupported mappings fail explicitly rather than choosing a convenient
+    edge.
+25. Public initial-state cut slots carry the canonical `Default` direction;
+    their signed fixed energies remain in the exact energy maps. This label
+    normalization occurs after fusion and preserves unfiltered residue IDs and
+    their order; it cannot supply missing denominator rank or re-sign a
+    numerator factor.
+

+  - retention of each term's selected exact numerator plan and matching payload.
+- `crates/gammalooprs/src/uv/approx/local_3d/residue_localizer.rs`
+  - projected soft-proposal selection before surface conversion;
+  - shared cut/hosting conversion for the winning payload and ordinary paths.
+- `crates/gammalooprs/src/cff/mod.rs`
+  - exact-source CFF assembly;
+  - retention and use of the planned exact-source numerator;
+  - physical cut and surface projection;
+  - unioned physical-owner support with additive raised-edge representatives.
+- `crates/three-dimensional-reps/src/generation.rs`
+  - generalized residue, finite-pole, and lower-sector CFF generation from the
+    supplied exact occurrence bounds.
+
+## Production acceptance checkpoint
+
+The retained 2026-08-31 10x campaign passes all four physical DD/TT
+acceptances (`4/4`) after exercising orientation-local 3D, explicit-sum 3D, and
+projected local 4D where the acceptance compares routes. Pulls are signed
+differences from the published target in units of the Monte Carlo error; ratio
+pulls include the LO uncertainty. These are historical measurements, not a
+fresh validation of the current tree. The converted `epem_a_ttx` acceptance
+compares complex magnitudes, so its pass alone does not certify the signed
+result or overall phase. The direct `gamma* -> t t~` test separately retains
+fixed signed LO and graph-NLO component checks.
+
+| Acceptance | 10x LO result | 10x NLO result | Graph and ratio evidence |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| direct `gamma* -> d d~` | `0.5068703962 +/- 0.0025987972` (`+1.449 sigma`) | `0.01966009810 +/- 0.00053595339` (`+1.424 sigma`) | `GL0=-0.03132123586 +/- 0.00023922726` (`+0.729 sigma`), `GL2=+0.05112479005 +/- 0.00046213299` (`+1.584 sigma`); `alpha_s/pi` pull `+1.141 sigma` |
+| converted `e+e- -> gamma* -> d d~` | `0.1950499744 +/- 0.0010326753 pb` (`+1.479 sigma`) | `0.007824189766 +/- 0.000340601513 pb` (`+1.630 sigma`) | signed MC components `GL0=-0.01996339254 +/- 0.00015479207`, `GL2=+0.02786745983 +/- 0.00028425324`; no separate published component targets; `alpha_s/pi` pull `+1.453 sigma` |
+| direct `gamma* -> t t~` | `2.901968994 +/- 0.015639978` (`+1.641 sigma`) | `0.2079169992 +/- 0.0042953541` (`+1.489 sigma`) | `GL0=-0.1443600613 +/- 0.0035809931` (`+0.669 sigma`), `GL2=+0.3522770605 +/- 0.0023720361` (`+1.687 sigma`); paper-ratio pull `+1.037 sigma` |
+| converted `e+e- -> gamma* -> t t~` | `0.3307052414 +/- 0.0018004843 pb` (`+1.603 sigma`) | `0.02356890542 +/- 0.00056839205 pb` (`+1.058 sigma`) | summed-graph integration has no persisted GL0/GL2 rows; paper-ratio pull `+0.685 sigma` |
+
+The converted DD graph components are closure diagnostics, not separately
+published observables, so this design does not assign them artificial targets.
+All LO integrations used 100,000 samples; the direct DD NLO used 400,000, the
+direct TT graph rows used 400,000 each, and each converted NLO central slot used
+200,000.
+
+The scalar LU 15-case matrix covers the same three production routes with local
+UV, integrated UV, and threshold counterterms all enabled. As retained
+pre-reversal evidence, its 2026-08-31 `dev-optim` / `test_gammaloop` rerun passed
+`15/15`, with `235` skipped, in `70.438 s`. The restored post-CFF direct route
+requires fresh validation after subsequent source changes. Four cases in that
+historical run used an f64-input `1e-14` unit-scale fallback. Current nonzero
+comparisons require finite values and precision-scaled relative agreement;
+only an exact source-zero certificate permits a separate absolute bound.
+
+## Validation map
+
+The most relevant focused tests are:
+
+| Layer | Test or fixture | Protected property |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Local-4D term parsing | `term_projection_preserves_complete_factorized_values` | Complete reconstruction with repeated powers, distinct wrappers, outer Taylor sums and positive numerator denominators; no storage-count requirement |
+| Real Taylor projection | `dod_one_triangle_keeps_separate_denominator_topologies` | DOD1 retains natural `(1,1,1)`, `(2,1,1)` and `(1,1,2)` denominator topologies with factorized numerators and no manufactured clearing factors |
+| Exact graph | `exact_source_preserves_the_complete_cubic_propagator_contour` | Complete signed cubic-pole contour and physical ownership |
+| Exact graph | `exact_source_owner_relabeling_preserves_residue_rank_and_cut_provenance` | Owner-invariant exact residue and loop rank, distinct energy provenance, and unioned physical cut support |
+| Exact graph | `exact_source_keeps_source_instantiated_domains_and_masses_separate` | Source-component and UV/cograph separation |
+| Exact graph | `exact_source_normalizes_opposite_spelling_inside_one_power_chain` | Normalized `Q/-Q` signatures on one source-routed chain |
+| Exact graph | `exact_uv_component_inherits_source_minor_and_rejects_wrong_provenance` | Multi-loop UV source-minor incidence and validation |
+| Exact graph | `exact_source_routes_a_hard_uv_row_modulo_the_soft_cograph_span` | Quotient-space solve chooses only the unique sign on source-fixed endpoints |
+| Exact graph | `exact_shifted_factor_reversal_preserves_projected_affine_maps` | Reversing shifted-denominator order preserves the complete projected residue |
+| Exact graph | `exact_uv_triangle_cached_and_uncached_residues_agree` | Cached and uncached complete residues agree for the base and every locally dotted owner |
+| Exact graph | `exact_uv_source_retains_a_non_vacuum_two_point_shift` | Pure-external crowns preserve a non-vacuum two-point boundary |
+| Numerator plan | `assignment_plans_preserve_owner_domains_and_complete_factorized_values` | Every proposal retains fixed/derived domains, sufficient energy capacity and the complete factorized numerator across sums, powers and multilinear functions |
+| Sign mapping | `exact_energy_bounds_keep_original_on_canonical_occurrence_across_routing_signs` | Original factors retain their base owner across routing signs |
+| Sign mapping | `denominator_derived_dispatch_composes_each_occurrence_routing_sign` | Dispatched derivative-created factors preserve signed physical hard momentum |
+| Fixed-owner sampling | `exact_energy_mapper_uses_selected_fixed_owner_sample_with_uv_mass` | The selected occurrence sample is consumed before its physical UV-mass on-shell replacement |
+| Dispatch proposals | `assignment_plans_preserve_owner_domains_and_complete_factorized_values` | Every bounded proposal retains fixed owners and exact factors |
+| Dispatch and cache parity | `bounded_exact_cff_dispatch_preserves_owner_contour` | Complete selected-plan and cached/uncached functions against an independent contour |
+| Exact CFF | `exact_cff_cubic_uv_rewrite_matches_production_convention` | Analytic cubic pole, quadratic rank, and input-order invariance |
+| Exact CFF | `exact_cff_uncancelled_powered_denominator_matches_lower_source` | Dotted cancellation with odd numerator |
+| Exact LU | `exact_cff_uncancelled_powered_denominator_matches_lower_lu_residues` | Same identity for the complete fixed-cut residue functional |
+| Shared CFF | `cff_repeated_occurrence_bounds_preserve_equivalent_physical_numerators` | Complete equivalent physical numerators across every `Q/Q/-Q` bound distribution |
+| Amplitude acceptance | `scalar_amplitudes_match_across_local_uv_routes` | Local 3D/local 4D equivalence, including native Arb comparison |
+| LU acceptance | `raised_cut_numerator_cancels_one_propagator_in_both_orientation_modes` | `q^2-m^2` cancellation in all three routes |
+
+Together these tests cover parsing, source-backed graph construction, canonical
+relabeling, sign handling, factorized rank planning, generalized-CFF contact
+sectors, exact analytic
+residues, local-3D/local-4D equivalence, and LU raised cuts. No single numerical
+process test is being used as a substitute for the structural invariants.
+
+## Design conclusion
+
+The essential distinction is:
+
+> Original source edges recover the known UV/cograph skeleton and retain
+> physical provenance; normalized denominator algebra defines the
+> owner-independent rational occurrence graph, while numerator factors are
+> assigned according to certified physical EMR provenance.
+
+Canonical `D(Q)=D(-Q)` normalization is safe because owner labels remain in
+energy provenance and cut-support metadata rather than contaminating the
+rational residue, while the raw routing sign remains separate data used to
+reconstruct the physical numerator. Raised-wrapper subdivision supplies the
+correct number of residue variables. The physical cut projection unions all
+owners of an algebraic channel and then adds raised-line representatives, so LU
+compatibility does not cost provenance. Explicit crown hedges preserve
+non-vacuum boundaries, and post-construction Graphica relabeling supplies
+deterministic cache identity without any topology inference from Kirchhoff or
+incidence matrices. The bounded search keeps the numerator factorized and
+chooses fewer native map rows among its certified proposals. Because the same
+selected plan controls both CFF generation and evaluation, the construction
+extends to higher powers,
+nested self-energies, disconnected UV components, LU residues, and multi-loop
+sources without a process-specific patch.

# Independent collective-forest oracle audit

Read-only audit of the two collective-region tests in `crates/gammalooprs/src/uv/hedge_poset.rs`, their concrete DOT fixtures, region classification, typed local-4D products, and `local_4d::uv_limit`/`t`/`Graph::uv_rescaled`. No Rust edits, Cargo invocation, jj mutation, or prefix-workspace change.

## Recommended fixture-specific value oracle

The two-component test may compare the sum of all computed local coefficients covering `U=A union C` with

`(-T_U) I + (-T_U)(-T_A) I = -T_U(1-T_A)I`.

Here the vacuum bubble A has DOD 2 and the vacuum triangle C has DOD -2. Taylor subtraction through A's superficial degree leaves a remainder with negative DOD; vacuum parity in this fixture improves it to at most -2. The product with C therefore has strictly negative combined DOD and has no divergent coefficient for `T_U` to retain. The complete mixed collective correction vanishes. The expected **atomic** term should be checked nonzero; the expected **sum** must not be required nonzero.

For the three-component fixture, A and B both have DOD 2, C has DOD -2, and U has DOD 2. The sufficient complete-value oracle is

`(-T_U)(1-T_A)(1-T_B)I`

with the four independently constructed proper prefixes: root, A, B, and the product A*B. Each prefix is a strict subset of U, so the construction needs no zero-quotient Taylor call. The two disjoint bubble operators commute because the actual fixtures factorize across vacuum cycles connected only by bridges. The mixed AC contribution vanishes as `T_AC(1-T_A)I=0`; likewise BC. Those cancellations persist after multiplying by the untouched disjoint factor, or applying an enclosing linear `T_U`. Consequently the additional AC/BC forest branches cancel in complete values and need not be enumerated individually by this fixture's oracle.

This justification derives from factorization, the Taylor remainder degree, and linearity. It does not derive the expected term catalogue from `Wood`, `TraceKey`, or cache contents.

## Independence and limits

Building the expected four prefix values directly with the existing typed product API and Taylor operator tests the forest traversal/composition against independent composition of the same public mathematical primitive. It does **not** independently prove the Taylor implementation itself; the owning local-4D algebra tests remain responsible for that boundary.

Comparing the complete value deliberately permits any internal representation that sums to it. This fixture does **not** certify that every canceled atomic/nested forest is stored separately, nor its multiplicity, map count, traversal order, or trace depth. A completely omitted canceling pair cannot be detected by a zero-value oracle and should not be claimed as detected. The nonzero atomic expected term establishes a nontrivial mathematical cancellation; it is not evidence that an actual stored atomic node exists.

For these concrete fixtures there are no nonzero crown shifts. Erasing momentum provenance, substituting the full-graph common loop chart, unwrapping `GS.den` to its complete propagator, normalizing dots, and collecting factors is a valid way to compare complete coefficients. This must remain fixture-specific: arbitrary nested sources can retain hard/soft ownership and shifted chart information that cannot safely be erased before their exact reconstruction certificate.

All signs come from the existing `uv_limit`, which stores `-T`. A direct product of the two signed bubble coefficients already supplies the positive two-subtraction sign; no additional forest parity should be applied. Preserve typed sectors until the final common-chart value comparison.

## Why the general 8-versus-12 catalogue was not certified

If one declares A, B, AC, and BC to be elementary proper regions and imposes only pairwise disjoint-or-nested compatibility, there are twelve proper sets: any subset of {A,B}, together with none, AC, or BC. In that purely combinatorial rule, the pairs {AC,B} and {A,BC} are valid even though their union is U.

That rule cannot automatically be imported from ordinary connected renormalization parts into this code's disconnected collective-region extension. A different, nested-set convention forbids incomparable members whose join is itself an atomic building block. The standard definition is stated by Bergbauer, Brunetti and Kreimer in *Renormalization and Resolution of Singularities*, Definition 4.4, page 29: https://www.esi.ac.at/preprints/esi2244.pdf . Applying that convention to an assumed atomic family {A,B,AC,BC,U}, with AB factorized, would exclude four sets and leave eight. This is a conditional comparison, not a claim that this repository has established that building-set model.

`uv_limit` rescales the whole current region even when the given cover equals it; a zero quotient does not by itself mean the operator is zero. Therefore silently adding such operations, or declaring them invalid solely because the poset lacks self-edges, would both be unjustified ways to select an expected catalogue.

The simplified four-prefix oracle avoids that unresolved general catalogue issue because the concrete vacuum fixture's mixed terms cancel. It is sound to test the resulting complete value and explicitly state this coverage limit. No failing test was changed during this audit, and no runtime result is claimed.

# Core stack reconciliation and complete review record

Inputs: main 39561014, raised-energy 91142139, phase-fix 32f27225, review payload ending ce6654cc. Reviewed the main-to-reconciled disk changes, with original remote/review trees consulted at conflicts. This agent did not mutate jj history; root owns reconstruction and validation.

## Reconciliation

Resolved all 29 owned conflict blocks in eight files. Preserved independent repeated occurrences, per-occurrence capacities/cache keys, bounded comparison by actual native generated source-map count, single-pass generation, and both shared-contour and physical-phase conversions. Rational values remain coefficients until conversion to GammaLoop symbolic outputs. Retained exact source certificates and complete factorized numerators.

Direct local/integrated replay retains remote ordering: integrated localization runs before local Taylor replay, since it registers surfaces needed by the local path. `run_local` borrows `&self`. `run_integrated` accepts `IntoIterator<Item=(Atom, &SuBitGraph)>`, preserving the owner of every integrated factor before multiplication. The kernel scales only the included owner's tagged mass; disjoint owners stay frozen and partial overlap/malformed owners return errors. Owner tags are stripped only on the output copy. Root migrated hedge-poset callers.

Projection coordinates are one `Option<(LoopMomentumBasis, ExactUvSubLmbFrame)>`; exact options belong to the Exact variant. There are no independently nullable coordinate/frame values or temporary compatibility shims. Removed a stale test argument after the existing `localized_orientation_terms` signature migration, and removed the unused source-test FeynmanGraph import.

Preserved remote owner-local interpolation. The former review assumption that positive/negative routing samples must be opposite separately in every interpolation row was invalid for independent occurrences. Tests now compare complete mapped contours and exact owner-local factor certificates.

## New correctness fixes and owning commits

### Commit 3: source adapters, planning, and reconstruction

- Energy cap addition/scaling and polynomial exponent conversion used unchecked usize arithmetic. Existing planning/analyzer APIs now return their existing Result channel; `EnergyDegreeOverflow` propagates through callers. Intermediate envelope costs use u128. The regression `overflowing_polynomial_degrees_return_an_error` checks rejection and the representable boundary. No new helper layer was introduced.
- Exact source momentum coefficients accumulated in i32. They now accumulate with checked i64 arithmetic and checked final i32 conversion through `GraphIoError::Source`, preserving large transient cancellations while rejecting unrepresentable final routings. `exact_momentum_signatures_reject_overflow_and_preserve_cancellation` covers both outcomes. The shared review widened public residual maps to Vec<i64>; the source consumer migrated atomically.
- `select_indexed_cff_residues` could index an empty raised group and accepted zero powers/unknown surface IDs. It validates every right/left/LU group before selection. Existing malformed-input coverage now exercises all three invalid forms on all axes. A pre-existing synthetic fixture using ID 0 with an empty surface cache was given its actual surface before any runtime failure; mathematical expectations did not change.

### Commit 4: UV profiling

- `UVProfileFixedRay::from_flat_components` accepted NaN/infinite directions and squared extremely large/small finite components. It now rejects nonfinite components and normalizes after dividing by the maximum component, using f64 hypot at this intentional f64 interface. Existing fixed-ray tests cover f64::MAX, the smallest positive subnormal, and nonfinite components/norms.
- Both profile entry points now reject finite exponents whose generated powers of ten are zero or nonfinite. `profile_rejects_unrepresentable_scale_ranges` tests amplitude and cross-section entry points.
- Profile magnitudes use hypot instead of sqrt(re²+im²), avoiding false zero/infinity from intermediate squaring. Existing fit coverage now includes normalization 1e200 and 1e-200 with the independent slope -1.
- A missing LU fit with zero samples plus NaN/infinity could receive the vanishing-fit exemption. Existing fit-status accumulation now invalidates that exemption if any sample is nonfinite. The complete pass/fail report regression requires a missing_fit failure for mixed zero/nonfinite samples.

### Commit 6: integrated adapter tests

The affine routing and nested-vacuum adapter tests no longer constrain VakintExpression's term-vector length/index, topology spelling, or prop numbering. They compare the entire recovered rational integrand, including powers 127/128+ and fixed external dot products. Independent Vakint review covers all integrated production changes; see its separate report.

## Behavioral-test review and cleanup

- CFF generation: cached/uncached and every certified dispatch strategy compare full signed contours. Removed private cache mutation, count/order thresholds, row zips, and enum-ownership assertions. Production raised poles compare complete selected residues for every supported CutCFFIndex.
- Expression/surface adapters: compare complete mapped factorized values and exact symbolic differences, not Atom node kinds or printed canonical expressions.
- Assignment planning: the existing `planned_candidates` certificate now checks all proposals for valid owner/provenance destinations, sufficient declared capacities and complete numerator reconstruction. A matrix of 13 expressions across three candidate domains replaces optimizer-specific load distributions/tie-break counts. No new reusable helper was added.
- Exact source tests: independently reviewed all 36 original tests. Complete cubic contour -3/(16 E^5), rank-reduced one-propagator -1/(2E), temporal dotted bubble +1/(4E), all-orientation mapper certificates, and the full GL04 T2 numerator/denominator certificate remain. Removed first-row and private coordinate/table/layout locks.
- Local/projected UV: compare complete selector-materialized integrands, Taylor expressions, all hosted terms, cached/uncached results, and independently signed contours. The quartic dispatch test uses -3 i/[32 (2pi)^3] at E=2 for every proposal. Removed private host sequences, cache/proposal counts, AST shapes, exact local-state/leaf counts and frame storage checks. Four redundant term-projection tests became one seven-expression reconstruction matrix.
- Finalization: zero sectors are verified as complete zero integrands for allowed residue keys, not empty private sector maps.
- Later CFF tests: independently read all 16 original tests through EOF; 14 remain after removing two redundant synthetic ownership-metadata tests. Retained complete mixed-component factorization, GL24 order-one quartic UV limit, left/right and scalar physical phases, 0–4-loop signed stored/direct bubble contours, tadpole/attached-bubble contours, and exact theta -1/12. Exact Rational-to-Arb fixture constants replace lossy f64 construction. See the independent report for detailed oracle changes.
- Non-approx UV: removed the test-only `includes` method and its mirror test; default selection is exercised by the full divergent-cycle inventory. Profile tests no longer prescribe fallback basis order/counts where the same physical cycles suffice. Export tests now sum all returned physical terms and all production values rather than requiring a single root row. UV tests compare complete factorized values instead of Atom::Mul layout. Report, selector, persisted schema fields and complete physical cycle inventories remain outward contracts.

## Rust patterns and effectiveness / KISS

- Type aliases and re-exports share one generic CFF engine. Extension traits adapt foreign shared types to GammaLoop symbols without duplicate algebra; callers explicitly import required traits.
- Rational coefficients encode the exact scalar domain. Atom conversion is explicit at symbolic boundaries, eliminating canonical-string number parsing and symbolic numeric ambiguity.
- Paired options and variant-local data rule out incoherent state without wrapper hierarchies. Typed final integrands make the finalization boundary visible to forest/evaluator callers.
- Immutable assignment plans carry ownership, provenance and capacity into reconstruction. This is essential to odd-numerator correctness; tests are free to accept any certified optimal layout. The machinery is complex because independent occurrences and exact off-shell routing are distinct mathematical constraints; adding another compatibility route would hurt KISS.
- Borrowed AtomView inspection avoids cloning during traversal. Owned Atom values are used for stored plans and reconstructed outputs. Explicit loops clarify fallible symbolic rewrites; iterator `collect::<Result<_>>()` gathers complete results before mutation.
- Checked conversions/Result propagation guard the integer representation boundary. Existing typed errors plus context identify invalid source data; no convenience panics or fallback saturation were added.
- IntoIterator of coefficient/owner pairs retains physical forest ownership before products, with lifetimes borrowed from existing nodes. Receiver mutability follows actual registration needs.
- BTreeMap/BTreeSet preserve deterministic inventories and public key sets. Determinism is useful; private map size and iteration order are not a mathematical contract.
- Profile workers clone evaluator state before sampling, and Rayon map_init gives each worker a local evaluator. Mutex locking is limited to cloning, so independent sampling is concurrent while errors cannot remove the process's production integrand. AtomicBool is a simple fail-fast signal; sequential fail-fast iteration preserves a completed prefix.
- Exact output oracles make tests shorter and more permissive of refactoring. collect_factors preserves graph numerator factorization. Large GL04/GL24 certificates remain justified: numerator parity, denominator multiplicity and forest ownership must be established separately.

Final cff/generation.rs one-/two-loop independent contour tests divide physical values by i^L after multiplying by (2pi)^(3L). In commit 3, before phase commit 5, those test conversion factors must instead be (-i)^L. # Proposed final commit-7 artifact inventory

**DRAFT.** This is an adoption/link plan, not a final passing certificate. The listed input hashes in the JSON are snapshot fingerprints only. No repository, jj, Cargo or PDF changes were made.

The four JSON bundles are assembled under `report-drafts/adoption/docs/architecture/`. The first frozen snapshot passed independent review. The refreshed snapshot retains all 217 previously reviewed compact contents and adds 40, covering the completed UFO/features and exact bridge-fix diagnosis/adoption. It contains 257 records from 291 locations and fingerprints for 185 external execution artifacts. `durable-bundle-refresh-delta.json` pins the old/new hashes; `durable-bundle-refresh-integrity-audit.json` verifies current source and artifact fingerprints. Bounded follow-up review, final runtime validation, artifact adoption and final PDF inspection remain pending.

## Intended new files

All nine targets are under `docs/architecture/`. Existing historical artifacts, including `raised-energy-cff-legacy-fixtures.md`, stay in place.

| Repository filename | Purpose | Required preparation |
| --- | --- | --- |

Preserve historical failed attempts separately from fixes. |

| `raised-energy-cff-stack-provenance.json` | Pinned original 42-commit inventory, jj operation checkpoint, scoped original/protected bookmarks, reconstruction boundaries and explicitly recorded later fixes/tree checks. | Assemble a durable snapshot without treating intermediate checkpoints as final. | `raised-energy-cff-stack-validation.json` | Machine-readable run ledger with exact argv/context, commit/tree identity, selected test identities/results, guard values, counts, durations, resource limits, log hashes and exclusions. | Embed or consolidate completed-evidence JSON records and overlap audits from the ledger; preserve failed and interrupted attempts. Replace active /tmp review references with stable IDs in the evidence bundle; preserve original recorded locations as metadata. Its own final file/diff hash belongs in the external receipt. |
| `raised-energy-cff-stack-evidence.json` | Durable evidence index containing named summaries, exact scope/proof categories and hash manifests. Preserve structured review manifests where they carry amendment chains; retain full review text when no equivalent durable structured scope exists. | Assign stable evidence IDs and consolidate the required review/audit summaries. Include final render verification and all non-log proof needed to understand coverage. Record its own checksum externally, not recursively inside itself. |

The companion JSON inventories each actual input path, its observed size/hash and the required transformation. The final PDF must be regenerated: the current draft PDF predates the current Markdown/Typst and must not be copied as the final report.

## Links and evidence locations

The audit found 17 existing forward links to `raised-energy-cff-stack-review.md` or `raised-energy-cff-stack-review-validation.md`; both targets are currently absent from the repository. Adopting those exact filenames resolves those links without editing the historical banners.

The three actual Markdown links in the new drafts and the one Typst link point to `raised-energy-cff-legacy-fixtures.md`. This is the correct repository-relative destination. It exists in `docs/architecture/` but not in the current `/tmp` draft folder; preserve the publish-relative link rather than replacing it with a temporary absolute path.

Most other dependencies are quoted evidence locators, not clickable links. `/tmp/raised-stack/validation.json`, `sources.json`, checkpoint files, `coverage-draft.json`, review manifests and render records need durable bundle references. Ambiguous bare names such as `evidence.json`, `selected-identities.tsv`, and `signed-acceptances.completed-evidence.json` need an explicit run/evidence ID. Root directory `raised-stack-adjust-api-boundary-review.json` likewise refers to a temporary manifest rather than an existing repository file.

Exact executed commands are historical data. Keep their real `/tmp` paths and binary locations inside the validation records; do not rewrite the argv to invented repository paths. The repository must contain enough summary and structured proof to assess the result without those long logs.

The current coverage snapshot uses 47 distinct first-hop review/audit input files across actual-diff, composed-amendment, aggregate and semantic-artifact proof categories. Their paths, hashes and affected records are listed in `final-artifact-inventory.json`. Preserve required nested amendment manifests when assembling the durable evidence bundle; this input-index audit does not claim another fresh code review.

## Avoid self-referential hashes

Commit 7 cannot contain its own final Git hash or tree, and a manifest cannot contain its own final checksum. Pin final functional commits 1–6 in the committed reports. Identify commit 7 there by its stable jj change ID and final bookmark. Hash the other report artifacts in the evidence bundle, and state explicitly where the bundle’s own identity is recorded.

After adopting and reviewing all final files, record commit 7’s final Git hash/tree, author/bookmark, complete final diff coverage, tree equality and the coverage/evidence manifest checksums in an external completion receipt and final response. This also closes coverage for the final manifests themselves without repeatedly publishing their previous versions’ hashes.

## Finish sequence

1. Finish or explicitly disposition the remaining findings and required approvals; finalize functional history and author metadata.
2. Refresh the source map, run ledger, scope/coverage records and pending-status prose. Preserve failures, interrupted attempts and exclusions.
3. Assemble the durable provenance, validation, coverage and evidence JSON files; replace active temporary evidence references with stable file/record references.
4. Generate the final Typst/PDF, compare all visible content and links, inspect every page, and record new render evidence.
5. Adopt the nine new files into both reconciled payload and commit 7; review their complete diffs and run the requested commit-7 gates.
6. Verify final tree equality and complete file coverage, then write the external final receipt.

Do not adopt live handoffs, scratch scripts, the stale PDF, build caches, copied executables, or the licensed environment wrapper. Keep the existing historical prose and its narrower evidence claims intact.

- All 42 original-source records have the expected fields and valid commit/tree/parent identifiers. The 37 remote and 5 review records match declared totals. Their 1,427 path entries have no within-record duplicates or absolute/traversal/newline paths. Source-pin entries agree with matching original-source commits. Original commit IDs are unique.
- The 6 observed functional-history nodes form the recorded parent chain. Prefixes 1, 2, 4 and 5 match the ledger's primary commit/tree; prefix 3 matches its last `later_validation_runs` entry. Its primary ledger pin intentionally retains older results at `417aef90`, whereas the observed history is at `1ec8fe52`.

Reviewed the complete `computed_uv_forest_process_export_uses_stored_sources_in_all_routes` test in `crates/gammalooprs/src/processes/process.rs` (original lines 1385–1838, 455 lines). Read its fixtures, preprocessing/generation, persistence, selection/regeneration, filesystem export inventory, and failure contracts. Read relevant existing export serialization and mathematical export-oracle code to reuse Graph parsing rather than introduce a new helper. No production edits or helper APIs were introduced.

The input already contained an earlier replacement of bincode/cache-byte assertions with consumed CFF expressions. This reviewer did not make or claim those earlier changes.

Resolved remaining storage locks: removed private supergraph/group-vector lengths, master flags, storage Option assertions, forest node count, and debug_dot string equality. Physical cut comparison now uses sets, so traversal order can change. Preserved public selection-plan ID remapping/removal reports, runtime lookup invalidation/regeneration, graph-name lookup, full expected cut/residue inventory, absence of removed exported graphs, mismatch rejection, and topology-only export behavior when computed source data is absent. The retained physical numerator and consumed CFF expression remain checked.

Each exported node DOT is now parsed using the existing Graph::from_string API. Its full exported numerator contributes to an aggregate per physical forest/residue; generated and loaded exports must have the same key set and exact factorized values. A nonzero exported value is required. This verifies consumable export artifacts instead of prescribing node grouping or IDs. Selection targets a different graph, so its export baseline is reset; its retained source numerator/CFF and cut inventory are independently compared to that graph before removal. Complete numerical export normalization is covered by the existing uv/export.rs regression, outside this edit's scope.

Rust/KISS: BTreeSet states unordered physical identity; BTreeMap groups complete outputs by their public forest/residue contract; existing parsing and Atom operations avoid custom inspection/serialization helpers. Comments are preserved and the new comment explains the persistence value boundary. Exact graph numerators remain factorized.

Validation: ran rustfmt on a temporary copy and copied back only the named test. Reviewed every changed hunk. Root runs compilation, Clippy and behavioral tests; this review claims no runtime pass. No known failing test was edited. Backups: /tmp/raised-stack-process-export-test-before.rs and /tmp/raised-stack-process-export-test-after.rs.

# Exact-source test review

Reviewed the entire `crates/gammalooprs/src/graph/three_d_source.rs` test module: original lines 3286–7230, including all 36 test functions, fixture closures, and the complete GL04 T2 numerator/denominator certificate. Read production only where needed to confirm existing output and error APIs. No production edits, jj operations, new helper APIs, or builds were performed by this reviewer.

## Changes

- Replaced the cubic-propagator test's private occurrence counts, graph-cycle shape and selector/cache storage assertions with the full independent signed contour `-3/(16 E^5)`, using the existing core-to-contour normalization. Physical owner projection and input validity remain checked.
- Replaced a rank-deficient source's chosen coordinate-matrix coefficients with its complete one-propagator contour `-1/(2E)`. The nonlocal algebraic input is explicitly diagnostic-only; it does not certify physical UV locality.
- Removed mirrored private occurrence tables from source-owner projection checks. Their public outputs still retain the complete expected owner set.
- Replaced stored raw-momentum/sign records in massless and external source parity tests with complete factorized numerator mapping for every generated orientation. Removed Atom `Mul`/`Add` node-count checks.
- Removed the derived-dispatch proposal's exact chosen rank distribution; retained mapped temporal/abstract values for all signed cases and explicit forced-candidate output contracts.
- Kept the full GL04 common-chart numerator identity, owner-role restrictions, denominator masses, domain, and complete multiplicities. Removed only redundant private occurrence-vector length checks.
- Removed triangle parity's canonical node numbering, occurrence-record/sign table and rank-vector constraints; retained complete direct-versus-exact mapped Minkowski residues and graph validity. Renamed the cache parity test to describe cached/uncached residue equality.
- Removed the dotted bubble's first-row interpolation sign requirements and rank-table equality. Retained the independent full temporal contour `+1/(4E)`, every row's owner-local mapped factors, and exact factor recombination. Crown and remote-owner passthrough now run over every generated row.
- Replaced a missing-candidate error-display substring check with the existing typed error variant and complete edge/degree payload.

## Retained contracts and Rust/KISS assessment

Parsed-source graph momentum balance, physical source incidence under contraction, external boundary presence, denominator multiplicity, physical-owner cut support, and fixed-versus-derived provenance eligibility are semantic reconstruction contracts; these are not cache/layout assertions. BTreeSet comparisons express ownership independent of traversal order. Synthetic mapper records are test inputs; assertions concern full mapped values, not their storage. Existing exact integer/rational maps and typed errors keep the semantic boundary explicit. Local closures define compact mathematical fixtures without creating reusable API layers. The GL04 certificate is necessarily detailed because separate numerator and denominator equalities prevent even-denominator symmetry from concealing an odd-numerator sign error.

All existing comments were preserved; new comments explain the independent cubic contour and the diagnostic-only rank fixture. The edit removes substantially more code than it adds. Factored graph numerators are not distributed for comparison.

## Validation

Ran rustfmt (edition 2024, skip_children=true) on a temporary file and copied only the test module back. Reviewed the full resulting diff against `/tmp/raised-stack-source-tests-before.rs`. Root owns cargo check, build, Clippy, and behavioral execution; no passing runtime result is claimed here. Newly introduced contour assertions and all-orientation parity must be included in that fresh run. No reported failing test was changed at edit time.

# Later CFF tests: independent review

Coverage: read the complete named region of `crates/gammalooprs/src/cff/mod.rs` from `selected_highest_pole_commutes_with_factorized_cubic_numerator` through the end of the module. This was 16 test functions and approximately 3,300 lines before edits. Every fixture, closure, numerical evaluator, assertion, comment and both terminal phase oracles in that region was read. Parent owns production and all earlier tests. No edits or formatting were applied before the named boundary.

## Findings resolved

- Mixed quartic-LU/MUV factorization asserted private energy-factor component counts, enum choices and degree-vector layout. Those preliminary locks were removed. The complete mapped mixed residue still compares against independently generated factors at Arb precision; aggregation now covers every returned sector.
- Connected-parent UV limits asserted fixed raw bridge tuples, component strategy enums, and an unused carrier permutation. Complete connected versus factorized physical results and the explicit raw-frame conversion remain; the implementation is free to choose equivalent internal frames.
- GL24 asserted hardcoded full orientation vectors and a fixed interpolation sample set. `gl24_selected_quartic_residue_uses_the_reduced_outer_frame` now maps and sums the complete selected order-one quartic numerator for root and outer, then compares the UV limit against the independently generated child times outer. The factorized numerical reference must be nonzero. This checks contributions that the old sample filtering could omit, so it particularly needs fresh runtime execution.
- Literal/nonliteral momentum parity no longer asserts repeated-group record counts, canonical keys or private raw signs before comparing complete nonzero Arb values.
- The former two-loop bridge-integer test is now `exact_two_loop_source_matches_the_signed_theta_contour`: both exact and ordinary complete results must equal the independent unit-energy theta contour `-1/12` after removing the spatial measure and physical `i²` factor.
- Unused one-/two-loop rank-capacity tests compare complete production values. Removed controls that required a specific incorrect manual application of private core-sign metadata to differ, and renamed the tests to their supported behavior.
- Removed two synthetic representation-only tests: `gamma_loop_prefactor_conversion_is_component_local_for_mixed_products` and `stored_production_cff_uses_typed_energy_factor_ownership`. They constructed/mutated private component metadata and required row counts/ordinal IDs. Their physical behavior remains covered by complete mixed-component factorization, unused-rank parity, and independent signed stored/direct scalar phase oracles.
- Compared public residue-index sets using BTreeSet, freeing map traversal order. Removed the powered-rational helper's private sector count/first-sector choice and summed complete values.
- Replaced every `from_f64` fixture constant in the owned region with exact Rational construction, including the `10^45` UV scale and the decimal point sequence. Precision now enters only when the exact values are converted to Arb.
- Removed unconditional terminal-contour stderr diagnostics; assertion errors already retain the full relevant values.

## Mathematical and behavioral coverage retained

Highest-pole commutation; repeated-channel polynomial division; both raised LU orders; values and first radial derivatives; odd temporal versus spatial spectators; cross-component Minkowski numerators; powered denominator cancellation and radial Laurent residues; physical owner distinctions; complete direct/exact projection parity; arbitrary-precision finite/nonzero checks; scalar coupling/model phases; 0–4-loop signed stored/direct bubble contours; terminal tadpole and attached-bubble contours; both standalone/embedded contexts; selector-complete sums. No graph numerator is algebraically distributed to establish a reconstruction identity. Existing comments were preserved or updated with their intent.

## Rust patterns / KISS

BTreeSet expresses unordered public sector identity. Borrowed iterator folds and existing mapping methods aggregate values without extra helper APIs; loops are clearer for fallible nested sums. Typed conversion methods remain production boundaries, but tests exercise resulting values rather than enum storage. Rational-to-Arb conversion makes exact inputs explicit. The long UV fixtures earn their length by comparing independent routes and derivatives; redundant preliminary generation and metadata assertions obscured those goals. This edit changes 101 added versus 624 deleted lines and leaves 14 functional tests in the owned region.

## Verification and limits

Ran rustfmt with edition 2024 and skip_children=true on a temporary full file, copying back only the named test region. Reviewed the before/after diff and the complete replacement GL24 and theta assertions. Backups are `/tmp/raised-stack-cff-later-tests-before.rs` and `/tmp/raised-stack-cff-later-tests-after.rs`.

Root owns cargo check/build/Clippy and behavioral execution. No runtime pass is claimed here. No failing test was reported when these edits were made. This review does not certify manual PySecDec integrations or code outside its named region.

# Commit 3 core failure triage (read-only, proposals awaiting permission)

Acceptance run: `/tmp/raised-stack/commit-3/behavior-tests.log`, actual commit `417aef90fb8e79562120bf6a3e08c9fc2561cb32`: 316 selected tests, 309 passed, 7 failed. This reviewer owns the five failures below. No failing test has been modified. Root handles the normalization and arbitrary-precision parameter-baseline failures separately.

## Cubic source contour

`graph::three_d_source::tests::exact_source_preserves_the_complete_cubic_propagator_contour`

First differing boundary: the production mapper deliberately keeps unchanged physical propagators in GammaLoop's OSE dialect. `GraphThreeDSource::exact_ose_replacements` returns E(edge) for a denominator whose source momentum/mass matches the graph; literal square roots are used only for rewritten exact denominators. This test builds unchanged edge-0 denominators but expects the literal square root from `FourDDenominator::on_shell_energy()`. The final `.together()` cannot identify an unrelated E(0) symbol with that square root.

Proposed test-only correction after approval: retain the independently derived clockwise contour -3/(16 E^5), and explicitly substitute the physical edge's OSE with `denominators[0].on_shell_energy()` into `contour` before the existing complete comparison. Alternatively formulate the same analytic oracle directly using `crate::utils::ose_atom_from_index(edge)`. Do not alter source signs or generated coefficients to address the dialect mismatch. No diagnostic replay of this test was needed to identify this explicit conversion omission. The corrected oracle still needs a fresh run; the finding does not certify the current contour coefficient.

## Direct residue branch homomorphism

`uv::approx::direct_3d::branches::tests::one_source_residue_map_is_a_homomorphism_for_all_factorized_factors`

The failed assertion prints complete actual/expected Integrands. At each cut order the actual value is `c*(2M+A)*(2M+B) + c*(3M+A)*(3M+B)` while expected is `c*((2M+A)*(2M+B)+(3M+A)*(3M+B))`, for c=5 and c=7. These values are identical; structural Atom equality sees the different location of c.

Proposed test-only correction after approval: normalize both complete Integrands using their existing `.map(|atom| atom.collect_factors())` operation before the explicit and localized comparisons, retaining the independent two-map substitution oracle and inactive-host zero result. This does not expand the numerator or constrain private branch/catalogue layout. A coefficient-distributed expected fold is another valid spelling, but the normalized complete-value comparison is less sensitive to that spelling.

## Assignment plans and local 4D term projection

`numerator::energy_degree::tests::assignment_plans_preserve_owner_domains_and_complete_factorized_values`

`uv::approx::local_4d::tests::term_projection_preserves_complete_factorized_values`

Both assertions subtract already factor-collected expressions and call `.is_zero()` on the newly formed result. For additive atoms, negation need not distribute, so even an identical normalized sum can leave an uncancelled `sum - (sum)` wrapper. Common-factor collection is not a canonical polynomial equality algorithm. Neither log prints the actual values at the failing input, so this is the directly identified assertion weakness, not yet a complete runtime classification of every fixture.

Proposed test-only correction after approval: first compare the two factor-collected complete expressions directly with `assert_eq!`. Preserve all owner-domain, capacity and reconstruction checks and each original input. If a genuinely different factorization remains, retain the values for a narrower exact identity or an explicitly limited exact-coordinate oracle; do not expand a graph numerator to make the test pass. Assertion messages should include the relevant input so a subsequent failure identifies the exact expression and route. No replay was performed because the existing tests provide no additional diagnostic output.

## Affine Vakint routing

`uv::approx::integrated::tests::affine_vakint_routing_keeps_external_momenta_fixed`

One explicitly authorized diagnostic replay of the preserved 417 binary was performed with only the Vakint trace enabled. It repeated the known failure and is **not** a new acceptance run, retry-to-pass, or addition to passing counts. No source or snapshot changed.

Command (cwd `/tmp/raised-stack/prefix/crates/gammalooprs`):

```sh
GL_DISPLAY_FILTER=off GL_LOGFILE_FILTER='[{#uv,#integrated,#vakint,#trace}]=debug' GL_TEST_LOG_DIR=/tmp/raised-stack/commit-3-at-417aef90/affine-diagnostic /tmp/raised-stack/run /tmp/raised-stack/commit-3-at-417aef90/gammalooprs-tests --exact uv::approx::integrated::tests::affine_vakint_routing_keeps_external_momenta_fixed --nocapture
```

The wrapper keeps snapshot updates and automatic retries disabled. Captured output: `/tmp/raised-stack/commit-3-at-417aef90/affine-diagnostic-replay.log`. Structured trace: `/tmp/raised-stack/commit-3-at-417aef90/affine-diagnostic/gammaloop-test-384496.jsonl`.

The first failing sign case (-1) reaches the expected topology `topo(prop(1,edge(0,0),k(0),mUV^2,3))`. The complete converted numerator is

```
(A+B)*(C+D) - (A+B)*C - (C+D)*A + A*C
A = dot(p(0),p(0))
B = dot(p(0),k(0))
C = dot(p(0),p(2))
D = dot(p(2),k(0))
```

This is exactly B*D, the independent oracle. External momenta are fixed correctly. The legacy Vakint preparation expands before the affine substitution, which explains this intermediate form; common-factor collection cannot rediscover the product identity. The topology-to-rational-integrand public conversion is correct. A production change to force the preferred test spelling is not justified. Because the test stops at the first assertion, the sign +1 case has not yet been freshly exercised by this replay.

This supplies sixteen complete exact values without distributing the graph numerator, and retains a symbolic denominator identity at every point. The 16-point grid determines the displayed multi-affine polynomial completely. The degree-at-most-one premise follows from the intended tensor structure here; if the revised test does not independently verify that premise on arbitrary erroneous output, it must be described as a finite exact-value regression rather than an unrestricted symbolic proof. A factor-preserving cancellation operation which proves the same identity would be preferable if the existing API supports one; no new helper/framework is proposed.

# Commit-3 normalization assertion: read-only triage and unapplied proposal

## Finding

`utils::test_utils::normalization` fails at the assertion introduced by the outward-test cleanup. The production `GS.linearize` callback itself is unchanged between `39561014` and actual prefix `417aef90`. It transforms the supplied `f(a+p+r)` into the exact complete expected expression `f(a)+f(p)+f(r)`.

A temporary standalone Rust probe invoked the production callback through the existing built `libgammalooprs-03fc7618a0c88e37.rlib`, linked against its matching `libsymbolica-47fe1906c816d603.rlib`. Both parse literals use `CARGO_CRATE_NAME=gammalooprs`, reproducing the original symbols' namespace. The probe printed:

```text
actual: f(a)+f(p)+f(r)
expected: f(a)+f(p)+f(r)
exact_equal: true
difference: f(a)+f(p)+f(r)-(f(a)+f(p)+f(r))
difference_is_zero: false
factored_difference: f(a)+f(p)+f(r)-(f(a)+f(p)+f(r))
self_difference: f(a)+f(p)+f(r)-(f(a)+f(p)+f(r))
```

Debug representations also match including every `gammalooprs` namespace. The assertion computes a factor-preserving subtraction, then asks whether that still-factored expression is literally the zero atom. Symbolica does not distribute the negative sum in this operation. Even subtracting the actual expression from itself leaves the same residual. `collect_factors()` does not change it. This is a test comparison error, not evidence of an incorrect linearization result or a namespace mismatch.

## Concrete proposal, NOT applied

`/tmp/raised-stack/normalization-outward.patch` changes exactly one assertion:

```diff
-    assert!((GS.linearize.call_args([expr]) - expected).is_zero());
+    assert_eq!(GS.linearize.call_args([expr]), expected);
```

The input and complete independent expected sum stay unchanged. The comparison uses exact normalized Symbolica expressions, with no expression formatting, traversal/count assumptions, numerical sampling, or graph-numerator expansion. No production helper or extra compatibility path is introduced. This belongs in owning commit 3. Repository guidance requires explicit approval before changing this known-failing test; the patch remains unapplied in main and all staged/live prefixes.

## Fresh actions and limits

The probe source is `/tmp/raised-stack/normalization-triage/probe.rs`; the final compiler diagnostics are `compile.log` and execution output is `run.log` in the same directory. It was compiled directly with the existing `rustc 1.97.0`, edition 2024, `--extern` arguments for the two built libraries above, the existing dependency directory and Cargo-emitted native link search paths. Output was `/tmp/raised-stack/normalization-triage/probe`. `CARGO_PKG_NAME` and `CARGO_CRATE_NAME` were both set to `gammalooprs`. Compilation and execution exited 0. No Cargo command was run, no default build target was written, and no existing Rust source/test was changed. An initial setup invocation failed because the newest rlib was removed during root's rebuild and `CARGO_CRATE_NAME` was missing; using the remaining built library and required namespace fixed the harness setup. That was not a behavioral test rerun.

This is focused execution evidence for the exact supplied oracle, not a fresh passing result for the repository test binary or whole commit. After approval and application, root must run the actual affected test and include it in the relevant prefix gates. Other subtraction-of-sums assertions may need the same mathematical triage before changing production or expected values; this report makes no blanket claim about them.

`/tmp/raised-stack/versions/prefix-1/.config/nextest.toml` now contains the minimal requested foundation changes: minimum nextest 0.9.115 with its existing explanatory comment; automatic manual-PySecDec exclusions for default, curated, CI and curated-CI profiles. This pass intentionally keeps baseline retry settings in the staged file; reconstruction execution must continue to enforce the user's zero-retry policy through its invocation environment.
